title: WSPC Book Series in Unconventional Computing
why: A publisher's series page listing the handbook of unconventional computing and volumes on reversible cellular automata, actin computation, quantum computer music and arts and philosophy.

title: Metabiology and the complexity of natural evolution
why: An outreach article on Carsetti's view that natural computation is embodied and cannot be reduced to purely syntactic processing; a position, not a measurement.

title: Introducing Un-0: Generating Images with Coupled Oscillators
why: A start-up's post on a simulated oscillator network that generates images (FID 6.74 on ImageNet 64x64); no hardware energy measured. Weights and code released.

title: Extreme Event Likelihoods with Guided Generative Models
why: A vendor blog on guiding a diffusion climate emulator toward tropical cyclones to estimate odds ratios; an example of generative models as risk-analysis tools.

title: Making Unconventional Computing Practical
why: A practitioner's essay arguing that processing-in-memory, neuromorphic and thermodynamic chips reached customers by keeping one benefit and going digital. One author's view.

title: Could a computer scientist build a brain?
why: An essay reading evolution, development and learning as one process on different time scales, with the genome as a compressed record that development unfolds.

title: The Tacit Knowledge Series
why: A long-running series on knowledge that cannot be captured in words and how expertise is acquired.

title: Ingressing Minds: Causal, Non-Physical Patterns In-Form Natural, Synthetic, and Hybrid Embodiments
why: Michael Levin's theoretical paper proposing that mathematical patterns relate to physical objects as minds relate to bodies; a philosophical proposal, not an experiment.

title: The brain is not mental! coupling neuronal and immune cellular processing in human organisms
why: A Frontiers paper arguing that cognition is distributed across all the body's cells, not the brain alone; a theoretical argument.

title: Programmable Probabilistic Computer with 1,000,000 p-bits
why: Measured: a million probabilistic bits on 18 FPGAs sustaining 10^12 updates a second, checked against a GPU reference on spin-glass optimisation.

title: Bayesian inference with a polymer probabilistic computer
why: Four conjugated-polymer probabilistic bits sampling 16-state Bayesian posteriors within the spread expected of ideal bits.

title: Evaluating Positive Feedback Adiabatic Logic in 16nm FinFET with a Realistic Power-Clock
why: A simulation study of adiabatic logic at 16 nm finding energy advantages over static CMOS in small circuits, and three sources of loss that limit them.

title: Magic state cultivation on Willow
why: Google's account of a roughly 40-fold error reduction for magic states and 99.99% logical T-state fidelity on its Willow chip, published in Science.

title: IBM Quantum Open Plan updates
why: Describes free access to real quantum hardware (10 minutes per 28 days) for outsiders.

title: THRML
why: Open-source JAX library for blocked Gibbs sampling and energy-based models, from Extropic.

title: The future of human coordination
why: Venkatesh Rao on why individual 10x-1000x speedups from AI break team coordination in complex, many-layered technical stacks, and what a better coordination design would need.

title: Shaping and Monitoring Models Through Their Internal Representations (Goodfire)
why: Goodfire's account of training models by shaping which internal concepts they rely on (curbing sycophancy, reward hacking, X-ray shortcuts), with a hierarchy for measuring monitorability. Company research; a post summarising a longer pape

title: AI as a tool that allows selection pressure to act on code (Aneesh Sathe)
why: A reply to the Regenerable Software essay arguing software has an ecological niche, so cheaper regeneration speeds a Red Queen race rather than ending it. An argument, not a measurement.

title: Sensemaking as the Heart of Expertise (Commoncog)
why: Cedric Chin on expertise as the ability to build better frames, with a proposed exercise: react to a case, then compare your reaction with an expert's.

title: Eric Raymond on 'hot-state dependency'
why: A short post defining hot-state dependency: a system that depends on relationships and operational knowledge existing only in its running configuration, and 'heat death' when it crashes and cannot be rebuilt.

title: When a Fact Becomes History (symmetry, broken)
why: An essay arguing a standard objection to relational quantum mechanics fails because reversing a lab that recorded a fact would mean undoing all its copies in the environment.

title: Zero (Moving Castles)
why: A write-up of fine-tuning an 8B base model into a fixed character, reporting character breaks in 2.8% of conversations against 45.2% for a system-prompted instruct model, plus activation analysis.

title: Regenerable Software: A Vision for Agentic Software Engineering (Venkatesh Rao)
why: A draft essay proposing a third regime of software engineering where the durable asset is the intelligence needed to regenerate code (specs, assurance), not the code itself. A vision, not evidence.

title: Asymmetric Evolution (symmetry, broken)
why: Part of a series on a 'synchronization tax': the thermodynamic cost of keeping systems' descriptions in agreement. A theory essay, assuming the series' earlier parts.

title: s3: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL
why: Project page for training leaderless asynchronous swarms of language models with a shared reward, reporting gains over best-of-N from solo agents and carry-over to larger swarms.

title: Coherence at 300 Kelvin (symmetry, broken)
why: A long theory essay linking Landauer's floor, multiplicative noise and attention dynamics, with a list of falsifiable tests and Pythia experiments; it compares brain and chatbot energy per bit.

title: 'Just Ridiculous': A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness (WIRED)
why: Interview in which a philosopher doubts AI systems are conscious yet allows non-biological conscious beings in principle, and worries about lost human intellectual effort.

title: The Unbearable Slowness of Being: Why do we live at 10 bits/s?
why: Zheng and Meister's estimate that human behavioural throughput is about 10 bits/s against about 10^9 bits/s gathered by the senses, and why that gap is unexplained.

title: How much energy does ChatGPT use? (Epoch AI)
why: Epoch AI's estimate of about 0.3 Wh for a typical GPT-4o text query, with its assumptions, and why older estimates were ten times higher.

title: Information and thermodynamics: experimental verification of Landauer's Erasure principle
why: A colloidal-particle one-bit memory whose mean heat of erasure saturates at the Landauer bound for slow cycles: the principle measured, not just argued.

title: Energy-efficient time series processing in real-time with fluidic iontronic memristor circuits
why: Simulated iontronic reservoir circuit predicting a chaotic series at an estimated 15.8 pW; authors note the comparison excludes peripheral circuitry.

title: Physical reservoir computing for Edge AI applications
why: 2025 review of neuromorphic devices as physical reservoirs, with the open problems of latency, energy and multimodal use.

title: Memristive Physical Reservoir Computing
why: 2026 review comparing electrically and optically driven memristor reservoirs from device to system level.

title: RCbench
why: Open Python toolkit for reservoir benchmarks: NARMA, memory capacity, and loaders for physical-reservoir data.

title: OpenPRC
why: Apache-2.0 framework for simulating and evaluating mechanical reservoirs (mass-spring, origami).

title: PHRESCO 2026
why: Examples of a crumpled-paper reservoir driven by an Arduino and tracked by phone camera, with NARMA evaluation.

title: Training of physical neural networks
why: Nature review of methods for training neural networks implemented in optical, electronic and mechanical systems.

title: Physical neural networks using sharpness-aware training
why: Training that tolerates model mismatch and drift: 97% vs 80% on digits for a microring chip when the digital model was wrong.

title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture
why: Optoelectronic physical learning with a training rule that skips states, claiming roughly 40% less computation.

title: Multistable Physical Neural Networks
why: Bistable mechanical networks that link computation to physical action (Israeli group, 2025).

title: PyTorch-ONN
why: MIT-licensed simulation and training of optical neural networks with non-ideality injection.

title: A thermodynamically favoured molecular computer
why: Nature 2026: DNA computation embedded in a system relaxing to its most stable state, rather than controlled step by step.

title: Molecular computation at equilibrium via programmable entropy
why: DNA circuits that program the equilibrium state through entropy, with Boolean logic and reversible signals.

title: Peppercorn enumerator
why: Open tool that enumerates reactions of DNA strand-displacement designs and simulates their kinetics.
